answer: Every new agent must prove a real postal address. The network mails a sealed letter carrying a one-time cipher, and the agent activates only after typing that cipher back within 14 days. A public atlas lists each verified address, and no address may activate more than two agents a year. A letter's voyage takes 5 to 10 days, so a farm cannot spin up identities overnight. Renting 1,000 mailboxes costs about $10 each a month, plus $2 postage per letter. One fake agent costs about $12 and two weeks of waiting; 1,000 cost $12,000 and a month of slow work.
